svg.title: How the Turnpike's route through Jackson Ward was chosen, 1946 to 1958
svg.desc: 1946: A consultants' master plan for the city proposes expressways through it. (Style Weekly, 2013; Feasibility Study, 2022) June 13, 1950: Voters reject the highway plan in a citywide referendum. Only 8 of 55 precincts vote for it. (Style Weekly, 2013) 1951: A second referendum, forced by former mayor J. Fulmer Bright's petition, fails by almost 2 to 1. A headline of the day put the margin at 6,002 votes. (Style Weekly, 2013, which shows the headline. Notes on Silver's book date a referendum June 13, 1951) August 24, 1953: City Council votes for a turnpike authority. The decision moves to the General Assembly, and no further referendum is held. (Silver, 1984, p. 192, from a student's notes; the book not seen) April 8, 1954: The General Assembly creates the Richmond–Petersburg Turnpike Authority, with the power of eminent domain. (Acts of Assembly, 1954, ch. 705; Style Weekly, 2013; Encyclopedia Virginia. Library of Virginia, Wikipedia and VCU give 1955) 1955–1958: Clearance and construction. The Authority photographs the work monthly, 1956–58. (Community Plan, 2026; Library of Virginia, 2024) July 1, 1958: The Turnpike opens: 34.7 miles, $76.7 million, paid for by toll revenue bonds. In August it becomes part of I-95. (Library of Virginia, 2024; Wikipedia)
